body: The Eye of Judgment is Sony's PlayStation 3 card-battle game, first released in North America on 23 October 2007. A PlayStation Eye camera watches physical cards placed on a printed three-by-three playmat, recognising their codes and presenting their creatures on the television. The player handles an ordinary card while the game supplies the animated battle and its rules. The arrangement makes the table part of the console's playfield. A strategic choice has a visible physical location, connecting the card in the player's hand to the creature occupying a space on screen.

The objective is to occupy five of the nine fields, making control of the small board more important than simply attacking every opposing creature. Players take turns introducing creatures and spells, choosing where each card can best contribute. The camera reads the placement, so the orientation and position of a physical object belong to the digital match. A small number of spaces keeps the whole contest visible at once. The challenge comes from recognising which field matters next and which card should be committed to holding or contesting it.

The release helped introduce the PlayStation Eye, with bundles including the camera, stand, mat and cards needed to establish the tabletop view. Further sets arrived in 2008, expanding the collection and associated systems. The hardware gives the game a particularly clear purpose for image recognition: it connects a physical collection to a rules-driven animated contest. Instead of using the camera mainly to show the player, The Eye of Judgment asks it to recognise the player's decisions on the table and bring those decisions into the world displayed by the console.
